To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) Monolithic CdZTe detectors can be used to achieve good energy resolution for medical and small-animal imaging, (2) the electrode pitch must be optimized with respect to material properties and thickness to achieve the best energy resolution, (3) the energy resolution of the detector can be further improved by electronic correction methods, (4) the appropriate correction method depends on the material.

monolithic CdZT detectors can be designed with a good energy resolution for various thickness and material transport properties, and that the best energy resolution is obtained for a detector thickness of 5 mm with a 1.7 mm pitch.

monolithic CdZTe detectors with optimized electrode geometries and thicknesses can achieve excellent energy resolutions and detection efficiencies, and that electronic correction methods are necessary to reduce the energy resolution tailing.

the design and characterization of high performance CdZnTe detector for medical applications.

the design of CdZnTe monolithic gamma-ray detectors for small animal imaging, the optimization of their performances, the correction of the electronic noise, the study of the charge transport properties and the development of new detectors.
the development of a new generation of CdZnTe detector for gamma-ray imaging, which will be optimized to be used in medical and small animal applications.
